cases.name: normal
cases.detail: one JSON document; both tables; single snapshot identity; scope check: no credentials/env/business tables in output

cases.name: lock conflict
cases.detail: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE blocker held; --lock-timeout-ms 500 refused the collector bounded (<5s, stderr LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR lock timeout); blocker kept its lock; zero collector connections/transactions/queries survived (pg_stat_activity residue empty after excluding blocker and fixture backends); retry after release succeeded

cases.name: connection failure
cases.detail: real in-container connection refusal (PGPORT=1 forwarded to the fixture container psql); bounded <15s, LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR

cases.name: garbage output
cases.detail: non-JSON psql output → LEDGER_COLLECT_ERROR; stdout never a plausible document

cases.name: server-side statement kill
cases.detail: statement_timeout=400ms with pg_sleep(30): server cancelled (57014 canceling statement due to statement timeout), transaction aborted, no sleeping query and no idle-in-transaction survived

cases.name: server-side lock kill
cases.detail: lock_timeout=400ms under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE: canceling statement due to lock timeout; blocker unaffected

boundaries.note: defaults in the collector; verification exercised the same code paths with shortened values

guards.dedicated_database: test refuses any database outside ^ledger_collect_ BEFORE connecting (phoenix_erp probe refused)
guards.same_instance: the URL database must exist on the specified container AND both views must report the identical server identity before anything runs
guards.staging_prod_transport: the staged SINGLE-file collector is actually RUN through its prod channel (docker compose exec db) against the fixture in scripts/ci/ledger-collection-staging.test.mjs
